findings.problem: The F1 repair fixed the SIGNAL SHAPE but silently changed the ADMISSION threshold, so the filed false positive still routes and a new one appeared. `evaluateComplexityGate` now pushes exactly one 'C' when its own sub-signals reach C_SUBSIGNAL_MIN=2 (correct, my measurement confirms signals are never C1/C2/C3), but the same edit set `trigger = explicitFlag || signals.length >= 1`, whereas the frozen contract says `trigger = (matchedSignals >= 2) OR anyExplicitFlag` (MATCHED_SIGNAL_MIN=2 remains exported and is now unused by the trigger). Measured consequences on the settled revision: (a) 'Check the test, build the package, verify the output.' => signals ['C'] => trigger true => routeDecision 'provision' — the exact sentence my t18 F1 filed, which the review criterion says must NOT stage a team; (b) 'align migrate refactor audit' (signal B alone) => trigger true; any single D (plan artifact) also triggers. So the round's headline claim (false positive closed) is contradicted by measurement, and two single-signal classes (a verb list, a plan artifact) bypass the two-signal bar that the frozen contract still declares. I CONFIRM the writer's mathematical argument: the false-positive sentence and frozen complex #1 have IDENTICAL frozen sub-signal profiles (B<4, C1<3, C2>=3, C3>=3 => C only), so no rule over the frozen signals can admit complex #1 and reject the sentence. The resolution is therefore captain-level, and the writer asking for sign-off instead of silently tuning is the right behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: One explicit captain decision, then make code, contract and evidence agree: (A) ACCEPT the widened trigger — restore `MATCHED_SIGNAL_MIN` usage becomes a documented contract amendment (`trigger = (anyC >= 2-of-3) OR explicitFlag OR any other single soft signal`) plus a trigger-rate re-measurement on ordinary prompts, because single-signal routing means any three-verb sentence stages a team; or (B) KEEP the frozen >=2 trigger — then the frozen complex prompts #1 and #3 are unreachable and the contract's frozen prompt set must be revised (the contract itself says testPrompts may not be silently re-tuned, so this needs a deliberate amendment); or (C) change the C sub-signal definitions so complex #1 separates from a plain verb list. Do not ship the current combination: code says >=1, contract says >=2, and the review's own counter-example assertion fails.
